convention: The hull box reaches the hull and turret roof; sights, antennas and roof guns are dressing within 0.3 m (bulky) or 0.15 m across (thin); the pivot sits at the centre of the turret ring (a fixed howitzer mount: its trunnion); the muzzle sits at the real barrel length. Box length covers the body (hull plus any armoured turret overhang), centred on the box origin.

thresholds.note: Slice 07's guesses, kept: every fix row below clears them by a wide margin or is named as borderline. muzzle_reach_m is added by lane F-C (the slice set none for muzzles).

width_m.source: Jane's Tanks and Combat Vehicles, M2 Bradley entry (issuu scan): width 3.61 m, height to gunner's sight 2.972 m, to turret roof 2.565 m; one35th.com M2 data: hull top 1.9 m, turret roof 2.565 m (with the armour tiles)

height_m.source: Wikipedia M2 Bradley (9.78 ft): the gunner's sight per Jane's (2.972 m)

turret_roof_m.source: Jane's Tanks and Combat Vehicles, M2 Bradley entry (issuu scan): width 3.61 m, height to gunner's sight 2.972 m, to turret roof 2.565 m; one35th.com M2 data: hull top 1.9 m, turret roof 2.565 m

measured.note: The photo reads the turret's side-armour edge from a low, close camera: an upper bound, 0.1-0.2 m over Jane's roof. Jane's governs.

model_glb.note: 3.057 m is the commander's independent viewer (M2A4) or the hatch ring; neither is dressing today.

verdicts.why: 3.61 m with the armour tiles; the art under-fills it (3.44 m), art-only.
2.98 m is the gunner's sight. The art's roof is already 2.537 m.

dressing_conflicts.why: Over the 0.3 m bulky allowance once the roof drops; slice 15 decides how sight heads are held (see decisions.md).

notes.why: The front fender (bradley.py:73) and the lower skirt panels and applique tiles at the nose run past the hull outline; slice 09 track_fender and side_skirt, adopted in slice 26. The frame's length and width match the published figures.
